milestone.description: ARCHITECTURE.md §17 M2: one member — nav grid, A*, task board, executes a dig order. Exit gate: order a dig, the member paths to it, digs it, the task completes, and 300 unreachable tasks posted at once neither freeze the sim nor blow the §13 budget. Proved headless in CI. 14 tasks, 19 dev-days estimated, ~25 with contingency.
milestone.title: M2 — Member, nav and task board

tasks.body:
A* needs to know which cells are walkable without asking Unity or reading tile sprites. ARCHITECTURE.md §8 says it plainly: bake per-cell nav flags when a chunk's tiles change — walkable, ladder, tube, requires-suit — so pathfinding and region detection both read one cheap array.

- [ ] Add a nav-flags array to the Kea.Core grid (one byte per cell, alongside the existing cell storage)
- [ ] Rebake a chunk's flags whenever its tiles change (hook the same dirty-chunk signal the mesh rebuild uses)
- [ ] Cover all four flag kinds: walkable, ladder, tube, requires-suit
- [ ] Unit tests: flag a cell solid → walkable clears; dig it out → walkable returns

Done when: editing any tile re-bakes only its chunk's flags, and a test walks the flag array to confirm each kind.
tasks.title: M2-01 Bake per-cell nav flags on chunk change

tasks.body:
This is the single cheapest performance win in the whole design, and the one that prevents the genre's classic failure: everyone freezing because 300 unreachable tasks are being pathfound every tick. ARCHITECTURE.md §8 rule 1 — flood-fill the walkable graph into region ids, rebuilt incrementally on tile change, and reject agent.Region != task.Region in O(1) before any pathfinding.

- [ ] Flood-fill walkable cells into region ids (same incremental pattern as the §5 room machinery)
- [ ] Rebuild only affected regions on tile change, never the whole grid
- [ ] Query API: regionOf(cell), sameRegion(a, b)
- [ ] Tests: seal a chamber → new region id appears; reopen it → regions merge

Done when: a sealed-off chamber reports a different region id, and region lookup is a single array read.
tasks.title: M2-02 Walkability regions with incremental rebuild

tasks.body:
ARCHITECTURE.md §7 gives members special permission the buildings don't get: at 20–100 agents, per-agent state machines are affordable, so favour readability over flattening. But two rules still bind: entity references are integer handles plus a generation counter (never object references — they break save/load), and agents are data the systems iterate, not GameObjects with Update().

- [ ] Agent struct arrays in Kea.Core: handle id + generation, cell, region, state, current task ref
- [ ] Spawn exactly one member; despawn recycles the handle with a bumped generation
- [ ] Stale-handle test: hold a pre-despawn handle, confirm it resolves to nothing, not to the recycled agent
- [ ] No MonoBehaviour, no Update(), no GameObject per agent — placeholder rectangle rendering comes from the snapshot like everything else

Done when: one member spawns with a valid handle, despawns cleanly, and a stale handle is provably dead.
tasks.title: M2-03 Agent entity: handles, not GameObjects

tasks.body:
Threading first would mean debugging the algorithm and the threading at the same time. ARCHITECTURE.md §8 wants A* on the grid with a worker thread eventually — but the algorithm itself gets built and proven single-threaded first, over the M2-01 nav flags, with unreachable goals returning cleanly instead of hanging.

- [ ] A* over nav-flag walkables (4- or 8-directional per the nav grid's movement rules)
- [ ] Admissible heuristic, path output as a cell list
- [ ] Unreachable goal returns empty, fast — no exception, no infinite loop
- [ ] Unit tests: open field, maze, sealed goal, start == goal

Done when: the maze tests pass and a sealed goal returns empty in bounded time.
tasks.title: M2-04 A* on the grid, single-threaded first

tasks.body:
The hard rule from §8: never path synchronously inside the tick — one bad request spikes a frame. Pathfinding moves to a worker thread (Kea.Sim job over the Core grid data), results are consumed the following tick, and the agent keeps walking its current path while the new one computes, so the visible latency is ~50ms.

- [ ] Request queue sim → worker, result queue worker → sim, both drained at tick boundaries
- [ ] Results consumed the tick after they arrive, never the same tick
- [ ] Agent keeps walking its old path while a repath is in flight (no stopping dead every repath)
- [ ] Determinism check: same grid + same request order → same path, headless (seeded, no Unity Random anywhere)

Done when: a repath request visibly resolves one tick later and the agent never stalls waiting for it.
tasks.title: M2-05 Pathfinding on a worker thread, results next tick

tasks.body:
Most path requests in this genre are repeats — forty members pathing to the same dig site. §8 says cache paths keyed by (start region, goal cell) and invalidate on nav-grid change in the region. Note the key uses the M2-02 region, not the start cell: same-region starts share cache entries.

- [ ] Cache keyed (start region id, goal cell), storing the cell list
- [ ] Invalidate entries whose region had a nav change since they were cached
- [ ] Hit/miss counters exposed for the debug HUD later (store them now, display in M11)
- [ ] Test: path once (miss), path again (hit), dig a tile in the region (invalidated → miss)

Done when: the hit/miss test passes and a dug tile provably evicts the affected entries.
tasks.title: M2-06 Path cache keyed by region, invalidated on change

tasks.body:
The pull model is the heart of §8 and the thing M2 exists to prove: buildings and systems *post* tasks, agents *pull* them. The struct is specified exactly — Task { Type, TargetCell, Priority, RequiredSkill, ReservedBy, ReachabilityRegion } — including the region field that makes the O(1) rejection in M2-09 possible.

- [ ] Task struct with exactly the specified fields, stored in a board array in Kea.Core
- [ ] Post API for systems (starting with a test poster — real posters come with construction and dig)
- [ ] Reserve/claim/release semantics: one agent per task, release on handoff puts it back claimable
- [ ] Stale-task expiry hook (post + expire run at divisor 2 per the tick table — expiry policy itself can stay trivial: drop completed/cancelled)

Done when: a test posts 300 tasks, one agent reserves exactly one, and release makes it claimable again.
tasks.title: M2-07 Task struct and board post/claim API

tasks.body:
The scoring formula is specified in §8 — score = priority × skillAptitude × personalPriorityWeight / (1 + pathCostEstimate) — and so is the philosophy that matters more than the formula: RequiredSkill is a skill *domain* for scoring and progression, never a class gate. Every reachable member may take a normal task. Only real constraints (missing equipment, sealed room, injury, unreachable path) may hard-reject.

- [ ] Implement the scoring formula exactly as specified
- [ ] skillAptitude + personalPriorityWeight as data the formula reads, not hardcoded per type
- [ ] No hard class gates: an unskilled reachable member scores low but is never rejected
- [ ] Tests: skilled agent outscores unskilled on matching work; unreachable agent loses to a farther reachable one once regions gate (M2-09)

Done when: the formula tests pass and no code path rejects a task for lacking a skill.
tasks.title: M2-08 Task scoring, aptitude without class gates

tasks.body:
The second affordability rule in §8: do not score every task for every agent every tick. Re-evaluate one agent per tick round-robin, plus immediately on task completion. At 10 Hz with 40 agents every agent reconsiders every four seconds — indistinguishable from smart, 40× cheaper. And the region check from M2-02 runs first, so unreachable tasks never reach the scorer.

- [ ] Round-robin: one agent re-scored per agent-update tick, plus instant re-score on any task completion
- [ ] Region pre-check before scoring: agent.Region != task.Region rejects in O(1), no pathfinding involved
- [ ] Counter for scorer invocations per tick (for the M2-12 freeze test to assert against)
- [ ] Test with 300 tasks × N agents: assignments happen, scorer cost stays flat per tick

Done when: completion triggers instant reassignment and per-tick scorer calls stay constant as tasks scale.
tasks.title: M2-09 Amortized assignment: round-robin plus on completion

tasks.body:
The tick table (§3) is authoritative: task board posts/expires at divisor 2, agent update (needs, assignment, movement, work progress) at divisor 2 — and divisors sharing a parity must be phase-offset, agents on tick % 2 == 0, buildings on % 2 == 1, or every 4th tick costs triple. This task wires M2's systems into that table instead of freelancing the schedule.

- [ ] Task board system at divisor 2, agent update at divisor 2, phase-offset per §3
- [ ] Agent update per tick: needs (stubbed to idle-work for M2 — real needs are M9), assignment pull, movement along the current path, work progress on arrival
- [ ] Movement consumes the M2-05 path: advance along cells at the agent divisor, request repaths through the worker queue
- [ ] Tick-order test: assert board ran before agents on even ticks (read-set/write-set discipline from §3)

Done when: the member visibly walks a computed path at game speed and the phase-offset test passes.
tasks.title: M2-10 Agent update at divisor 2, phase-offset per tick table

tasks.body:
M1-13 proved a dig order end to end — but with no member to execute it. This task closes the loop the milestone is named for: a player dig order enters the command queue at a tick boundary (§3 system #1), becomes a dig task on the board, the member pulls it, walks there, works it through a progress rate, and the tile flips.

- [ ] Dig task type: TargetCell + progress, work rate per agent-tick on arrival
- [ ] Command queue accepts the player's dig order and posts it at the next tick boundary (never mid-tick)
- [ ] Arrival → work → tile flips dug → task completes and releases
- [ ] Placeholder-rectangle rendering of the member moving and the tile changing comes free from the M1 snapshot path

Done when: ordering a dig with the member idle ends with a dug tile and a completed task, no cheats.
tasks.title: M2-11 Dig execution: order, walk, work, complete

tasks.body:
The failure §8 names explicitly: 300 unreachable tasks must not freeze anyone. This is the test that proves the M2-02 region gate earns its keep — posted sealed-chamber tasks get O(1)-rejected while reachable work continues, and the scorer counters from M2-09 prove the cost stayed flat.

- [ ] Headless test: seal a chamber, post 300 tasks inside it, keep 1 reachable dig posted
- [ ] Assert the reachable dig still completes and tick time stays within the §13 budget
- [ ] Assert scorer invocations per tick did not grow with the unreachable pile
- [ ] Runs in the Kea.Tests.Bench harness so CI enforces it

Done when: the test passes in CI and fails if the region pre-check is bypassed (verify by toggling it off once).
tasks.title: M2-12 Unreachable-task freeze test (300 sealed tasks)

tasks.body:
M2's exit gate from §17: order a dig, the member paths to it, digs it, done. This task bottles that into a scripted headless scenario in the benchmark harness — the proof artifact for the whole milestone, rerun on every push.

- [ ] Scripted scenario: spawn member, order a dig across the map, run until the task completes
- [ ] Assert completion, assert path length within 10% of optimal, assert tick budget held throughout
- [ ] Wired into CI alongside the M1 breach scenario
- [ ] Update the §17 build-order table: M2 checked off with a link to the scenario

Done when: CI runs the scenario green and the §17 table marks M2 complete.
tasks.title: M2-13 Exit gate scenario: ordered dig completes in budget

tasks.body:
Small print so the milestone is actually finished: the tick-order table in §3 lists the two new systems at their divisors, §8's task-board and pathfinding subsections note any deliberate deviations taken during implementation, and the milestone description's estimates are corrected to what things really cost.

- [ ] §3 tick table updated with the M2 systems as built
- [ ] Deviations from §8 recorded next to the spec they deviate from (or explicitly marked none)
- [ ] Actual days-vs-estimate noted for the next milestone's planning

Done when: someone reading §3 and §8 cold gets the system as built, not as planned.
tasks.title: M2-14 Docs close-out: tick table and deviations
